original_value: This paper presents an integrated approach to plan smooth path for robots docking in unknown environments with obstacles. To determine the smooth collision‐free path in obstacle environment, a tree structure with heuristic expanding strategy is designed as the foundation of path planning in this approach. The tree employs 3D Dubins curves as its branches and foundation for path feasibility evaluation. For the efficiency of the tree expanding in obstacle environment, intermediate nodes and collision‐free branches are determined inspired by the elastic band theory. A feasible path is chosen as the shortest series of branches that connects to the docking station after the sufficient expansion of the tree. Simulation results are presented to show the validity and feasibility of the proposed approach.

result.paraphrase: This paper proposes an integrated method for planning smooth robot docking paths in unknown obstacle-filled environments. A tree-based path-planning framework with a heuristic expansion strategy is used to find a smooth, collision-free route; its branches are formed by 3D Dubins curves, which also serve as the basis for feasibility assessment. To improve expansion efficiency in obstacle environments, intermediate nodes and collision-free branches are selected using ideas inspired by elastic band theory. After sufficient tree expansion, the feasible path is obtained as the shortest branch sequence leading to the docking station. Simulation results demonstrate the validity and feasibility of the proposed approach.
